data.gender_notes: Rabindar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is born in a lotus flower, symbolizing purity and divine origin. The name Rabindar carries the meaning “Lotus-born” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Rabindar usually hope their child will grow to embody lotus-born and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the spiritual journey of the soul, born from the divine lotus of consciousness.
data.etymology: Rabindar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lotus-born.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rabindar total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rabindar carries rich cultural connotations in Hindu society, meaningful in both its syllables ‘Ra’ and ‘Bindar.’ The syllable 'Ra' is believed to be the root syllable of several revered Hindu deities such as Rama, Rudra, and Brahma. This association with divinity enhances the stature of a person bearing the name Rabindar.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rabindar is deeply rooted in spiritual consciousness, derived from the ancient Indian belief in being born amidst the purest and most divine elements – the lotus flower. The spiritual significance lies in the name's literal meaning - 'one who is born in a lotus flower.'
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rabindar: Radiant in the divine presence, embodying wisdom and compassion.

historical_references.reference: Rabindranath Tagore was a prominent Indian poet, playwright, painter, and philosopher in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He was a central figure in the Bengali literary renaissance and is often described as the 'Bard of Bengal'.
historical_references.context: Rabindranath Tagore is a significant figure in Bengali and Indian literature. He was a prolific writer and artist, and his works have had a lasting impact on Indian culture.

historical_references.reference: Rabindranath Tagore was born in Calcutta (now Kolkata), India, on May 7, 1861. He came from a prominent Bengali family and was educated at home until he was sent to England for higher education at the age of 17.
historical_references.context: Rabindranath Tagore was a prominent figure in Indian literature and culture. He was born into a prominent Bengali family and was educated both in India and England.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Rabindar is derived from the Sanskrit language and means 'servant of Lord Rama'. In modern times, the name Rabindar has gained popularity across various platforms. On Goodreads, Rabindar Nath Tagore is a renowned poet whose works are frequently read and recommended by users. On Spotify, Rabindragapali Sangeet, an album by Rabindra Sikhariya, is a popular collection of Rabindranath Tagore's songs. In educational settings, Google Classroom offers resources and tools for teachers to incorporate Rabindranath Tagore's poetry and teachings into their curricula.
